name: Card Casting
body:
The card casting class ability grants the ability to form a bond with a deck of playing cards, using them to unlock mystic powers. You have a maximum hand size, determined by the class that granted you the card casting ability. Playing a card caster requires one standard deck of 54 playing cards, with two jokers and four suits each with ranks of Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King. The player will use these cards to determine what abilities are available to the PC. The PC uses a similar deck as a spell focus, shuffling, drawing, and playing cards to activate his powers. You must bond with a deck before it can be used as a focus.

You must have a free hand to manipulate your deck and hand and to hold your hand of cards. The same hand can be used for both holding and manipulating.

Treat each spell card as a single use spell. Each deck has a tradition and each card lists relevant traits, range, area, targets, and durations.

A card can be in one of four places: in the deck, in your hand, in play, or discarded.

In the deck. At the end of your daily preparations and after any time you shuffle your deck, all your cards are in the deck. The deck is placed face-down. Normally, the only way to return cards to the deck is to shuffle all cards, though some abilities can grant other methods.

In your hand. Drawing cards from the deck into your hand requires you to draw them as a swift action. When you draw, you can take as many cards from the top of your deck as needed to reach your maximum hand size. Cards in your hand can be activated (“played”) with the actions required for the individual card, which counts as casting a spell. Cards are removed from your hand by playing them or by discarding them. Normally only cards in your hand can be played. Multiple cards can be played at one time, see Empowering below.

In play. Many cards have an instantaneous duration. Such cards are played, resolved, and moved to the discard pile immediately. When a card creates an effect that has a duration other than instantaneous, the card is laid face-up on the table. Such cards count against the number of cards you can hold in your hand. If such a card is empowered, the empowering cards are laid below it and also count against the size of your hand. When the effect ends, the card and any empowering cards are immediately moved to the discard pile and no longer count again the size of your hand.

Note that any ongoing spell card effect can be dismissed by discarding the card, which can be done as a free action on your turn, which moves the card to the discard pile, or by the deck being shuffled, removing all cards from play.

Discarded. Cards in the discard pile are unavailable for use. Normally, these cards will remain here until the deck is shuffled.

Playing Cards

These actions are used when casting card spells.

Draw. As a swift action, you draw a number of cards from the top of your deck up to the number required to reach your maximum hand size. If you have multiple decks, cards can be drawn from either in any combination.
Discard. During your turn, you can move a card from your hand or one card in play, with any empowering cards, to your discard deck. Removing a card from play ends the duration of the spell card’s effects. Discarding a card is a free action.
Shuffle. As a standard action, you can shuffle your deck. Take your entire deck (all discarded cards, cards in your hand, and cards in play) and reshuffle. All cards are now in your deck. This ends any ongoing card spells that you cast. You can shuffle a spell deck a number of times per day equal to your Charisma modifier. These uses are regained after completing a short rest or a long rest.
Empowering

When a card is played, additional cards can be played at the same time to empower it, granting additional benefits per the played card. This is part of the action to cast the spell; it does not cost any additional action.

Empowering cards must either be of the same rank as the played card or else be of the same suit and form a contiguous sequence starting or ending with the card to be empowered. For example, a 4 of hearts can empower 6 a 4 of spades, clubs, or diamonds, as they have the same rank. It could also empower a 5 of hearts or a 3 of hearts, as they form a sequence. Each empowerment benefit must be paid separately, though different benefits can be paid by more than one type of empowerment. For example, if you play the ace of clubs from the primal deck, you can empower it with a 2 of clubs to increase range and an ace of spades to increase the movement penalty.

Wild Cards

A card with the Wild trait—also referred to as a “wild card”— can function as being of any rank and of any suit when being used to empower another card.

Scaling Effects

Unless otherwise stated, any effect of a card that increases with level is based on the cartomancer’s class level rather than their total character level.

Putting it Together

As both the players and the PC are manipulating cards, there could easily be some confusion.

At the table. You, the player, have a standard 54 card deck, which is shuffled prior to use. The GM can ask to cut the deck after shuffling. When you draw, you physically draw the cards into your hand. Likewise, you keep a discard pile for discards. Cards that are in play are laid in front of you, face up.

In the game. You, the PC, keep your bonded deck in hand or in a readily accessible pocket or pouch. You draw, hold, play, and discard cards with one hand. Cards in play create visible spell manifestations, often with the suit of the card or images on the card manifesting as or around the spell effect. Discarded cards return to a convenient pouch or pocket. Cards in play can only be targeted as spell effects, not as objects. When a card in play is discarded, it returns itself over any range; you are not required to go and pick it up or otherwise retrieve it.
